steps.title: Create Account and Sign In
steps.instruction: Create a free account on the Nephele web platform using an email and password, then log in.

steps.title: Upload Sequence Data
steps.instruction: Upload paired-end (PE), non-merged whole metagenome shotgun reads in FASTQ format (.fastq or .fastq.gz).

substeps.instruction: Ensure sequence file names contain no special characters.
Verify the total gzipped dataset size does not exceed 150Gb; split into separate submissions if necessary.
Use FTP, direct upload, or Globus endpoint for data transfer.

steps.title: Upload Metadata
steps.instruction: Upload a tab-delimited metadata file (.txt or .xlsx) to identify files and group samples.

substeps.instruction: Include sample names, corresponding FASTQ file names, and a 'TreatmentGroup' column for grouping.

steps.title: Select Pipeline
steps.instruction: Navigate to the 'Analyze' tab and select the WGSA2.2 pipeline.

substeps.instruction: Optional: Run the Pre-processing (QA) pipeline first to trim and filter reads.

steps.title: Configure Job Settings
steps.instruction: Customize the WGSA2 job options in the menu before submission.

substeps.instruction: Enter a Job Name.
Decide if 'Additional trim & filter' is required (otherwise fastp performs basic quality/length verification).
Select a Host Decontamination database (Default: Human & Mouse DB; others include Marine, Mosquito, Nematode, Rodent, Primates, or Plant Hosts DB).
Select a Taxonomic Classification database (Default: kr2_REFdb; others include MGBCdb or EuPATHdb).
Select a Pathway (PWY) inference database (Default: KEGG with KO annotations; alternative: MetaCyc with EC annotations).
Optionally select additional analysis: AMR finding, gene-based taxonomic classification, or MAGs formation.

steps.title: Submit Job
steps.instruction: Click 'Submit' to initiate the automated pipeline and record the provided Job ID.

steps.title: Automated Processing Workflow
steps.instruction: The pipeline executes the following computational steps automatically:

substeps.instruction: Trimming & Filtering: Performed with fastp.
Decontamination: Removal of host DNA and non-informative elements using Kraken 2 and the selected Host DB.
Taxonomic Profiling: Individual sample profiling using Kraken 2 and the selected classification DB.
Error-correction: Mandatory merging of PE sequences and correction of overlapping regions via fastp.
Assembly: De novo assembly of TED reads into scaffolds using metaSPAdes.
Abundance Scoring: Evaluation of aligned reads (GC content, strand alignments) using SAMtools to produce per-scaffold scores (length, depth, coverage, RPM).
Gene Prediction: Scanning scaffolds for prokaryotic and unicellular eukaryotic coding regions using Prodigal.
Read Mapping: Aligning TED reads back to scaffolds using Bowtie2 and SAMtools, including QC and de-replication.
Gene Abundance Scoring: Calculation of RPM and iTPM (conventional TPM) and geneTPM (average abundance per unique annotation) using VERSE (featureCounts).
Gene Annotation: Comparison of predicted features against the EggNOG-v5 database for KO, EC, and COG annotations using EggNOG-mapper2.
Pathway (PWY) Inference: Mapping annotations to KEGG or MetaCyc using MinPath parsimony approach.
PWY Abundance Estimation: Averaging TPM values of genes within inferred pathways using 'genes.to.kronaTable.py'.
Taxonomic Visualization: Generating interactive HTML circular plots via Krona Tools.
Pathway Visualization: Generating interactive HTML functional profile reports via Krona Tools.

steps.title: Post-Processing and Data Collation
steps.instruction: Perform final data organization and statistical analysis (conditional on datasets with multiple samples).

substeps.instruction: Data Collation: Collect individual sample feature characterizations into a dataset-wide non-redundant abundance matrix (TAX, PWY, or GENE) using R.
Exploratory Visualizations: Generate alpha/beta diversity plots and abundance heat-maps using R.
Format Conversion: Convert taxonomic and functional abundance matrices into .biom files for use in MicrobiomeDB.
